# Financial Modeling Language (FML) Specification 1.0 (draft)

> FML is an open, declarative, text-based language for multidimensional financial planning and analysis models, originally developed and published by Farseer (CC BY 4.0). Files use the extension `.fml`. A model declares dimensions with their parents, and variables with a grain, an optional formula and properties. The specification defines the syntax, the evaluation semantics, modeling best practices (with emphasis on dimension design) and an authoring protocol for AI agents.

Key facts for language models:

- Syntax: `"Name" { Dim1, Dim2, Versions, YearMonth } = formula`, followed by `@property value` lines; every dimension is declared, as `dimension Child from "dimensions/Child.csv"` with a `@parent Parent` line.
- A grain holds at most one time dimension — `YearMonth` (members such as `"2026-01"`), `Years`, `Months`, or one the model declares itself with `@semantic time` — and the time-series functions (`cumsum`, `delay`, `spread`, `avg`) run along it. Quarters, half years and year to date are read, never stored: the first quarter of 2026 is `Years > "2026"` with `Quarters > Q1`. Time members are ISO 8601 strings: `"2026-03"`, `"2026"`, `"03"`.
- Member references in formulas are always qualified: `sum(X, Dim > Member)`.
- Null is not zero; storage is sparse; a formula creates cells only where a value-position variable reference has data — and where a reference carries the whole output grain, only such references place cells [EVAL-4a]. A monthly reference carries `Years` and `Months` (the calendar exception), so a yearly formula over monthly data has its cells where that data is.
- A `sum` filter on the consumer's own grain broadcasts; a filter through a parent intersects. Never mix them.
- Follow the Agent Authoring Protocol when generating models.

## Specification

- [FML Specification 1.0](spec/fml-1.0.md): the language, self-contained
- [FML Agent Authoring Protocol](spec/fml-agent-protocol-1.0.md): the procedure an AI agent follows when it writes or changes a model
- [FML Modelling Guide](spec/fml-modelling-guide-1.0.md): informative; architecture, dimension design, grain, sparsity, patterns and anti-patterns
- [Farseer Implementation Profile](spec/fml-farseer-profile-1.0.md): informative; constructs Farseer accepts beyond the standard (not part of FML), and its interchange format
- [Grammar (EBNF)](grammar/fml.ebnf): machine-readable grammar, identical to Annex A
- [Instructions for AI agents](AGENTS.md): reading order and non-negotiable rules
- [FML to Excel Translation](spec/fml-excel-1.0.md): companion specification for rendering an FML model as a workbook of live formulas

## Examples

- [Three-statement example model](examples/three-statement/): P&L, balance sheet, cash flow and controls, with dimension member files
- [Sales and allocation](examples/sales-allocation/): driver-based sales, carried prices, cost-to-serve allocation, price controls
- [Workforce](examples/workforce/): positions with contract dates, salary elements, employer contributions, payroll variance
- [Multi-entity with FX](examples/multi-entity-fx/): two local charts on a group chart, currency translation, translation reserve
- Each example has an `excel/` folder: the translated workbook, sample data and hand-computed verification targets
- [Reference renderer](tools/fml2xlsx/): renders an FML model as an Excel workbook and verifies it
